# Precision of `brevio-core scan` on open-source repositories: TypeScript and JavaScript

<!-- Generated by tools/precision_run.py from precision.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Run on 2026-11-06. The scanner checked 10 pinned repositories (ts-react-oss, language: TypeScript and JavaScript): 19,126 files and 3,350,731 lines. It reported 1,606 hits. The figures are for this corpus and this language only.

## Results

Precision is the share of sampled hits that are real problems, shown as the hits judged real of the hits judged. Up to 20 hits per rule were drawn at random (seeded), then read in their code.

| Rule | What it checks | Hits | Sampled | True | False | Precision | Interval |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R2.8 | No unsafe code or HTML sinks: no eval or new Function on strings; dangerouslySetInnerHTML only with sanitised HTML | 57 | 20 | 20 | 0 | 20 of 20 | 0.84 to 1.00 |
| R5.4 | No silent exception swallowing: log or surface errors; never use empty catch blocks | 78 | 20 | 15 | 5 | 15 of 20 | 0.53 to 0.89 |
| R6.3 | Deterministic condition waits: never use waitForTimeout/sleep in tests | 135 | 20 | 6 | 14 | 6 of 20 | 0.15 to 0.52 |
| R9.1 | No untyped escape hatches: no `as any` casts or `z.any()` schemas in production source | 987 | 20 | 20 | 0 | 20 of 20 | 0.84 to 1.00 |
| R9.2 | No silenced type errors: no @ts-ignore; every @ts-expect-error states its reason | 334 | 20 | 20 | 0 | 20 of 20 | 0.84 to 1.00 |
| R13.1 | Zero secret logging: redact passwords, tokens, API keys, and authorization headers | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | not judged |  |
| R18.1 | Meaningful image alternative text: informative images supply descriptive alt attribute | 8 | 8 | 7 | 1 | 7 of 8 | 0.53 to 0.98 |
| R18.5 | No click handlers on non-interactive elements: divs/spans with onClick specify role='button' | 7 | 7 | 6 | 1 | 6 of 7 | 0.49 to 0.97 |
| All | | 1,606 | 115 | 94 | 21 | | |

**These verdicts were recorded before the tool kept the name of the reviewer.** The results do not say who judged them, or whether one person did. Each verdict and its one-line reason is in [precision_sample.jsonl](precision_sample.jsonl), so anyone can check or dispute them (see Reproduce): read the line at the path in the repository at that commit.

The corpus is human-written code, so this is precision on human-written code, not on code an agent wrote. The interval is the Wilson score interval, 95% for the share of judged hits that were real, worked out from the two counts in the same row. With few judged hits it is wide, and the figure is rough.

## Review

Rules whose sampled precision is below 70%: R6.3.

| Rule | Review |
|---|---|
| R2.8 | New ID: these findings carried R2.5, whose title is the SSRF and timeout guard. Kept `stable`. Fixed: vendored folders, minified files and bundles are skipped; TypeScript declaration files (`.d.ts`, `.d.mts`, `.d.cts`) are skipped; test fixture assets are skipped; static literal eval probes in test files are skipped; and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with sanitizers (`escapeHtml`, `DOMPurify.sanitize`, `sanitizeHtml`) is accepted (2026-11-06). No sampled hit was judged false after these fixes. |
| R5.4 | Kept. Fixed: vendored folders, minified files and bundles are skipped. Left: unminified React and Vue builds that one repository keeps as test assets in a folder with another name; a project excludes them with `exclude` in brevio-core.toml. |
| R6.3 | Preview: it reports and never fails a scan. Most hits are deliberate waits in a browser-automation project's own tests (checking that nothing happens in a given time) and test sources written as strings. No small pattern fix is clearly correct: flagging a sleep only before an assertion that already waits would keep few of the real hits. Candidate for the maintainer to narrow or retire. |
| R9.1 | Kept. Fixed: comment lines no longer match. |
| R9.2 | Kept. Since declaration files are skipped (2026-11-06), three `@ts-ignore` comments in one Playwright `.d.ts` are no longer reported. |
| R13.1 | Rewritten: it flags known credential formats, a JWT, or a random-looking value bound to a secret, token, password or API key name, and leaves placeholders, public and publishable names, Stripe `pk_` keys and Algolia or DocSearch keys alone. It has no hit on this corpus, so no precision: the corpus holds no hard-coded credential. Its earlier false positives (public search keys, a storage entry name) are tests now. |
| R18.1 | Kept. Fixed: comment lines and test files are skipped. Left: a block-comment line that does not start with an asterisk. |
| R18.5 | Kept. Fixed: test files, and a handler that only stops propagation, are skipped. |

## Method

- The scanner is brevio-core's own code, run under `python -I`, so no file of the scanned repository can load code.
- Each repository is fetched shallowly at its pinned commit into a cache outside this repository. Its licence file is checked against the corpus.
- The scan reads whole files: `brevio-core scan --fail-on all .`. It skips dependencies, build output, vendored folders, minified files and bundles. No rule reads a TypeScript declaration file (`.d.ts`).
- The sample is drawn per rule with the seed `e35` from the hits in a fixed order, so the same hits give the same sample. The files quote none of the code: a sampled hit is stored with its repository, commit, path, line, rule, verdict and reason, and the SHA-256 of its line.
- Interval: Wilson score interval, 95%, on the hits judged for the rule. It is printed in the Interval column.
- Scanner: exported from harness commit `bbdb617fdb0f7553b295b7a1dc6f43925a369a05` with uncommitted changes; SHA-256 of the scanner's files `d11bdcf0ad03d4ec5fcf3eb103a60e386c036eb2e8ad61f97cc77e4d27ae4fe4`; Python 3.12.3.

## Reproduce

You need git and a Python that brevio-core supports; no package is installed. In a checkout of this repository, with `CACHE` and `OUT` two folders outside it:

```sh
python tools/precision_run.py --cache CACHE --out OUT --seed docs
git init -q CACHE/<owner>__<repo>
git -C CACHE/<owner>__<repo> fetch -q --depth 1 --no-tags <url> <sha>
git -C CACHE/<owner>__<repo> checkout -q --detach FETCH_HEAD
cd CACHE/<owner>__<repo> && python -I -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1]); from brevio.pipeline import core_cli; raise SystemExit(core_cli.main(sys.argv[2:]))" TREE scan --fail-on all .
```

The first command does all the rest; the others show what it runs for each repository, with `TREE` the root of this repository, the folder that holds the `brevio` package. It needs the network, because it clones each pinned repository; the scan runs on the cloned files. `--seed docs` starts `OUT` from the judged results in `docs/`, so the committed files stay as they are. A run keeps each verdict whose hit is still sampled, matched by the hit's ID and by the hash of its line, which the run reads again from the clone. A hit the run samples that has no verdict yet is listed with its surrounding lines in `OUT/precision_to_judge.jsonl`.

Compare `OUT/precision.json` with `docs/precision.json`. The date, the scanner's digest and the Python version differ by design; the hits and the figures per rule are what to compare. A figure that differs can mean that the scanner or a repository is not the one measured here; when you cannot tell, open an issue and attach both files.

To dispute a verdict, open an issue with the form "Dispute a precision verdict" and name the hit's `id` from `precision_sample.jsonl`. `SUPPORT.md` says when to expect a first response.

## Measure a corpus yourself

`tools/precision_corpus.json` can hold several corpora, each with a name and a language. Four steps, in order. The scan runs on local files, and a person judges the sampled hits.

**Pin.** Give each repository a name, a URL and a `ref` (a branch or a tag) in the file, then run:

```sh
python tools/precision_run.py --corpus-name NAME --cache CACHE --pin
```

With the network, this fetches each repository, writes the commit it found as `sha` and writes the licence it read from the licence file (MIT or Apache-2.0). It writes nothing when one repository fails.

**Run.** This scans the pinned commits and draws the sample. Without `--detail` it writes totals only: no count per repository goes into `precision.json`. The counts are kept in `OUT/precision_detail.json`, which a release does not ship. `--detail repository` writes them into `precision.json`.

```sh
python tools/precision_run.py --corpus-name NAME --cache CACHE --out OUT
```

**Judge.** For a row of `OUT/precision_sample.jsonl`, read its line in `OUT/precision_to_judge.jsonl`, then set `verdict` to `tp` or `fp` and write a one-line `reason`. Write your name in `reviewer`, or let this command write it on the judged rows that have none:

```sh
python tools/precision_run.py --corpus-name NAME --out OUT --rejudge --reviewer YOURNAME
```

**Publish.** This refuses, and writes nothing, while a sampled hit has no verdict or a verdict has no reviewer. Otherwise it writes the figures and this page, and the rule pages show them for the language of the corpus.

```sh
python tools/precision_run.py --corpus-name NAME --out OUT --publish --reviewer YOURNAME
```
